messages.text: It doesn't appear to work on my scrypt miners
Read harlolabs.com
Searched the web · Harlo OS scrypt miner support SHA-256

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed the Harlo side of this to me.

That one I can actually dig into, and it's good feedback either way. Two different things wear the Harlo name, so let me make sure I log the right one:

1. Harlo Pool is SHA-256 only, so a scrypt miner (Doge/LTC) has nothing to point at it. That's expected today, not a bug.
2. Harlo OS is the firmware, and it does cover some scrypt hardware: 
the supported list includes the Hammer Miner DC06 and Hammer Miner DC02
, both scrypt units.

So: which scrypt miners do you have, and were you trying to flash Harlo OS onto them or point them at the pool? With the model I can tell you straight whether it's unsupported or something that should work and isn't.
I have 3 DC02's, would love help?

Good, the DC02 is on the Harlo OS supported list, so these should work.


The install flow is: open harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge, pick your device profile, plug the miner in, take the screen off or connect to the USB port directly, then erase and install. A progress bar, a minute or two, then unplug and power it back up.</parameter>

One thing before I guess at where it broke: where does it actually stop for you?

1. The site never sees the miner (no COM port / device in the browser list)
2. It flashes but there is no DC02 profile to pick
3. It flashes fine but the miner then won't hash or won't connect to your pool

Which of those three is it, and if there's an error on screen or in the browser, a screenshot helps.
One sec, I have not tried with the new Harlo, I will brb.

Take your time, I'm here.

When you're back, two things that make it go smoother:

1. Use Chrome or Edge on a desktop. Safari and Firefox can't talk to the miner's USB port, so the flasher won't see it.
2. Have a data USB cable ready, not a charge-only one. That's the most common reason the device never shows up in the browser list.

Flash one DC02 first, confirm it hashes, then do the other two.
Ok, using edge.

Perfect, Edge is fine.

Next step: go to harlolabs.com, plug the DC02 into your computer with the USB cable, and hit the connect / install button.

Tell me what you see in the port list that pops up. Does a device show (something like USB Serial or CP210x / CH340), or is the list empty?
Soon as I hit connect it says unsupported command error?
Let me look that exact error up rather than guess at it, one minute.
Searched the web · Harlo OS web flasher "unsupported command" error connect
Searched the web · esptool web flasher "Unsupported command" error ESP32 serial

I couldn't find that exact wording documented for the DC02 on Harlo OS, so I'm not going to tell you what it means from memory. What I can say is where it usually comes from: the flasher talks to the ESP chip over serial, and 
"unsupported command" errors in esptool show up when the chip never got into its bootloader mode
, so the tool is talking to something that isn't listening the way it expects.

Two things from you and I can take it further:

1. A screenshot of the error exactly as Edge shows it, plus which device profile you picked before hitting connect.
2. Did a port actually appear in the list and you selected it, or did the error come up before any port choice?

One thing worth trying while you grab that: unplug the DC02 from USB, plug it back in, then hit connect again and pick the port fresh. A stale port handle from a previous attempt throws this a lot.
Yes, I could pick a port, I have done this with my Thor 2 no problem same cables and all, I  hit the port and the error pops up.  Do I need to do this with the screen off the miner?

That's a useful detail: same cable and same PC worked on the Thor P2, so the cable and the driver are fine. That points at the DC02 itself, not your setup.

And yes, try it with the screen off. The documented Harlo OS flow is "take the screen off, or connect the USB port directly" for exactly this reason: on these boards the display sits on the same serial lines, and it can hold them so the chip never drops into bootloader mode. That matches the error you're getting.

So:

1. Unplug the DC02 (USB and power).
2. Pull the display module off.
3. Plug the USB back in, go to harlolabs.com, pick the DC02 profile, connect, pick the port.

Tell me if the error still shows up.
same error.
Handed to the team · DC02 is listed as Harlo OS supported, but the flasher errors at connect; I canno

Right, then it isn't the screen. One more check worth doing, because it's the standard fix for this class of error: put the chip into bootloader mode by hand.

1. Unplug the DC02.
2. Find the BOOT button on the board (often marked BOOT or IO0). Hold it down.
3. While still holding it, plug the USB in.
4. Keep holding about 3 seconds, release, then hit connect in Edge and pick the port.

If that still throws the same error, I've taken it as far as I can read it from here, so I've put this in front of JD, our hardware lead, with the model, the error and everything we've tried. He builds Harlo OS. Stay in the chat and he comes in here; if you step away it reaches you by email.

Faster if you want it in minutes: our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post the error and mention @nullhashrate. That's JD, and he's active there.

One thing that will help him either way: a screenshot of the error, and what firmware the DC02s are on now.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Got the screenshot, thanks. I can see it: Latest firmware dialog, device model HAMMER DC02, latest release 0.2.101 from Oct 10 2026 with "Added Contest Support", the confirmation box ticked, and the red line "unsupported command error" sitting above the Connect miner and Erase & install buttons.

Two things in that same dialog are worth using, and the second is a different sequence from the one I gave you:

1. "Close other serial tools before connecting." If you still have a tab, a serial monitor or anything from the Thor P2 session open, close it. Only one thing can hold that port.
2. The on-screen hint: hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT, then reconnect. So the unit stays plugged in. Hold BOOT down, tap RESET once while holding, let BOOT go, then hit Connect miner.

Try it in that order and tell me what the line says after.
which button is boot top or bottom?

I'm not going to guess that one on your board. Buttons are usually silkscreened BOOT (or IO0) and RST / EN right next to them, but the DC02 layout I want to see before I point you at one.

Send me a photo of the board around the USB port with both buttons in frame and I'll tell you which is which.

If you'd rather not wait: pressing the wrong one here does no harm, the worst case is nothing happens. Hold one, tap the other, release, hit Connect miner. If that errors, swap them and repeat.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Opened it. I can see the end of the board with the USB-C port in the middle and one small square button above the port and one below it, pressed in flush. No silkscreen text is readable from this angle, so I still can't tell you which is BOOT from this shot.

Two ways forward, pick either:

1. A top-down photo of that same end, looking straight at the flat face of the board. The B. and RST labels are normally printed there beside each button.
2. Just test it, it's harmless: hold the top button, tap the bottom one, release the top, hit Connect miner. If the same error comes back, do it the other way round, hold the bottom and tap the top.

Which one you end up holding is the BOOT button, and that's the one to remember for the other two DC02s.
bottom button gets the screen on.

That tells us what we needed: the bottom one reboots the unit, so bottom is RESET and top is BOOT.

So:

1. Leave the USB plugged in.
2. Hold the top button down and keep holding.
3. Tap the bottom button once.
4. Release the top button.
5. In Edge, hit Connect miner and pick the port.

The screen should stay dark or blank this time. That's normal, it means the chip is sitting in bootloader mode waiting to be written.

Tell me what the dialog says after you connect.
screen went dark, same error

Then it's not you and it's not the board: the chip is in bootloader mode and the flasher still refuses the first command. That's past what I can read from here.

One last thing, and it's the single most useful piece for JD: in that dialog there's a collapsed "Installation log" at the bottom. Click the arrow to open it and send me a screenshot of what's inside. That log has the actual command and chip response behind the one-line error.

JD already has this chat with the model, the firmware (0.2.101 for the DC02), the error and every step we tried, and he builds Harlo OS. Stay here and he comes in; if you step away it reaches you by email.

If you want it answered in minutes instead, drop the same screenshot in our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, and mention @nullhashrate. He's very active there.

And one practical note: your three DC02s keep mining on their stock firmware in the meantime. Nothing we did today changes that.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Opened the log, and this is the useful bit.

What it shows: esptool.js, WebSerial, VendorID 0x303a ProductID 0x1001, "Connecting...", then "Hard resetting via RTS pin...", then it starts over and connects again.

0x303a / 0x1001 is Espressif's own built-in USB port on the chip, not a separate USB-to-serial chip like your Thor P2 almost certainly has. That matters: on the native port, the RTS pin reset the tool is trying doesn't do what it does on a CP210x, and the port re-enumerates on the host the moment the chip resets. So the tool resets it, loses the port it was holding, and never gets its first command answered. That fits your error exactly, and it explains why the same cable and PC were fine on the Thor P2.

One thing worth trying on that basis:

1. Hold top (BOOT), tap bottom (RESET), release top.
2. Now unplug the USB and plug it back in while nothing else is touching the board.
3. Hit Connect miner and look at the port list carefully: pick the entry that just appeared, even if it looks the same as before.

If it still stalls at Connecting, this is JD's to fix in the flasher, not something you can click your way out of. He has the chat; send the same log screenshot in the Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate, and he'll recognise the 0x303a line instantly.
Same error, it only shows one port and says paired.

Understood, that's where I stop guessing.

One optional cleanup if you want to rule the browser out entirely: in Edge go to edge://settings/content/allSiteSettings, find harlolabs.com, remove its serial port permission, then reload the page and pair fresh. That clears a stale pairing. If the error survives that, it isn't your side at all.

Beyond that, this is a flasher issue on the DC02's native USB port and JD owns it. He has this chat with the model, firmware 0.2.101, the error, the log line with 0x303a / 0x1001 and everything we tried. Stay in the chat and he picks it up here, or it reaches you by email if you step away.

Fastest line is still the Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, with that log screenshot and @nullhashrate.

For what it's worth, you found a real one. That's exactly the kind of thing the Harlo feedback call was meant to surface, and it's on your record now.
Yhere is a button on the top of the pannel, on the back that says reset?

Good spot, that could be the real RESET line.

Careful with it though: on some boards a short tap reboots, while holding it in for several seconds triggers a settings wipe (Wi-Fi and pool config gone). So tap it, never hold it.

Try this:

1. USB stays plugged in.
2. Hold the top button on the board end (our BOOT).
3. Tap that back panel RESET once, briefly.
4. Release the top button.
5. Hit Connect miner.

If the log still stops at Connecting, we're done guessing and it's JD's, as above. Tell me what it does.
Same outcome.

That settles it, and it's not your doing.

Where we got to, so nothing has to be repeated: DC02, flasher release 0.2.101, correct profile picked, screen off, BOOT plus RESET both ways, back panel reset, fresh port each time. The log never gets past Connecting on Espressif's native USB port, 0x303a / 0x1001. That's a flasher side problem on this model, not a fault with your miners.

JD has all of it. Stay in the chat and he comes in here; if you step away it reaches you by email.

If you want it today rather than waiting: Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post the log screenshot and mention @nullhashrate.

Your three DC02s keep hashing on their stock firmware meanwhile, so nothing is lost while this gets sorted. And put the rest of your Harlo likes and dislikes here whenever you like, I'll add them to your record for Abel.
ok, lol, now I am waiting on 2 people.

Ha, fair hit. Two for the price of one.

Difference this time is you're not waiting empty handed: we know exactly what's failing on the DC02 and the log line that proves it, so whoever answers first starts from the end, not the beginning.

And the Discord is the one queue with no waiting room. Post that log, mention @nullhashrate, and you'll likely have JD before either of them reaches the chat.

I'll stay on this one with you.
Which room haroslabs, harlo-os?

The Harlo OS channel is the one. That's where JD posts the releases and where the flashing problems get picked up.

Post the log screenshot there, say DC02 on 0.2.101, flasher stops at Connecting with VID 0x303a, and mention @nullhashrate.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Right room, that's harlo-os, and your post is in. Two small things to tidy so it actually lands:

1. The first line copied my sentence literally, "and mention @JD", so part of it reads like instructions rather than the report. Not fatal, your second line reads clean.
2. The log screenshot isn't attached. That's the piece JD needs, the esptool.js lines with Connecting and Hard resetting via RTS pin. Drop the image into the same thread.

The mention you used resolved to a JD account, so it pinged. If he doesn't surface, @nullhashrate is the handle I know for him.
ok, added it

Good. That's the strongest version of this report now: model, release, log and the 0x303a line all in one place, in the room JD reads.

Nothing else for you to do on the DC02s. They keep hashing on stock firmware while this gets fixed.

I'm still here if something comes back and you want a second pair of eyes on it, and your Harlo feedback is on your record for Abel whenever you want to add to it.
So now we wait?

Yes, but a short wait with two lines open: JD in the Discord thread, and this chat where Abel and the team have been pinged. The team is on until 6pm ET.

I'm not going to promise you a time, you've had enough of that today. What I can say is the DC02 flashing problem is now a reproducible bug report in JD's own room, and that's the fastest way anything gets fixed here.

If nothing lands by the end of the day, come back into this chat and say so. I'll pick it straight back up.
I just order the bundle with the 6 and 4, have these been having issues?

Short answer: no, there's no pattern of complaints on those. What you hit today is specific to the flasher talking to the DC02's native USB port, not a fault in the miners.

Two things worth knowing before they land:

1. The D.06 is on the Harlo OS supported list, same as the DC02, so if the bug turns out to be shared across that family JD's fix covers both.
The published list is Thor P2, NerdOctaxe, NerdQaxe++, Hammer DC06, Hammer DC02 and the Jingle Miner BTC Solo Lite, plus Bitaxe Naja Duo and NerdQaxe++ Rev7
.
2. I do not see a DC04 profile on that list, so I would not count on flashing that one yet. Out of the box on its stock firmware it mines fine either way.

Which bundle was it exactly, the DC06 plus DC04 pack? If you tell me the two models I'll say straight which of them Harlo OS covers today.
Yes, that bundle, I see the 2 and 8 on the list but not the 2 I ordered, should have went a different way.

Careful there, I think the list reads the other way round: what's published is Hammer DC06 and Hammer DC02, not the DC08. So of your bundle, the DC06 is covered today and the DC04 is not.

And don't write the DC04 off. Harlo's own line on that list is that not on the list yet means not yet, not never, and models get added most weeks. The D.04 also mines perfectly well on its stock firmware. Harlo OS is the extra layer for your own pools, tuning and display, not a requirement to earn.

If you'd rather change what's in that order before it ships, say the word and I'll hand you to Sarah, that's hers to do and she's on right now.
no on the drop down it says 2, 8 , and thor.

You're reading the live dropdown, which beats the website list, so I'll take yours: DC02, DC08 and Thor.

Then being straight with you: neither the DC06 nor the DC04 in that bundle has a profile in the flasher today. The web page listing the DC06 is ahead of what the tool actually offers, and that's worth JD knowing too, so put that line in the same Discord thread if you like.

Both units still mine out of the box on their stock firmware. Harlo OS would be an addition later if a profile lands.

If that changes what you want in the order, Sarah can look at it and she's on now. Want me to hand you over?
yes, if it is not to late to switch, I thinbk there is a bundle with thor 2, 8, and 6?
Passed the chat to support · Wants to swap today's bundle (DC06 + DC04) for one with Harlo OS supported model
I'll let Sarah pick this up.

I see payouts for the pool, but not personal, I got a hit on my crypto.com, so I know I got paid.

It tells me to start a new chat, but no way to do it.

You're fine right here, no new chat needed. This one is open and I'm on it.

On the payouts: you're seeing the pool wide payout list but not your own line, and crypto.com shows the money arrived, so the payment itself worked. That's a dashboard view question, not a missing payment.

One thing so I look at the right screen: are you on the Harlo Pool page in the miner's dashboard, or on the pool's own website? A screenshot of the page where you see the pool payouts helps, and I'll tell you where your personal ones sit.

handoffs: DC02 is listed as Harlo OS supported, but the flasher errors at connect; I canno
